name: Aloo Pyaaz ki Sabzi
subtitle: everyday dry potato and onion stir-fry, sharp with amchur and hing

ingredients.qty: 500g, boiled, peeled and cut into 2cm cubes
ingredients.note: boil them the day before if you can. Cold potato holds its shape
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free
the sourness is the point of this sabzi

prepNotes: Boil and cool the potatoes fully before cubing. Hot potatoes crumble in the pan and you end up with mash.
Slice the onion thick, in half-rings. It should stay in identifiable pieces, not melt into the potato.
Measure the spices into one small bowl before you start; the whole dish takes 20 minutes and the tadka moves fast.

steps.text: Heat the oil until it shimmers, then crackle the mustard seeds, followed by the cumin.
Add the hing and slit green chillies and fry 15 seconds.
Tip in the sliced onion and cook 6-7 minutes over medium-high heat until the edges brown but the pieces still have bite.
steps.tip: Stop while they are still slightly firm. Soft onion disappears into the dish.

steps.text: Take the pan off the heat, add the turmeric, chilli and coriander powders, and stir for 10 seconds in the residual heat.
Return to the flame, add the cubed potato and salt, and toss to coat every piece.
Fry 8 minutes over medium heat, turning only every couple of minutes, until the potatoes take on crisp golden faces.
steps.tip: Turning constantly breaks the cubes and stops any crust forming. Leave them alone between turns.

steps.text: Crush in the kasuri methi and sprinkle over the amchur, then toss and cook 1 more minute.
Stir through the coriander leaves and serve hot with methi bajra puri or plain roti.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. Reheat in a dry pan over medium heat for 5 minutes to bring the crisp edges back; it goes soft in the microwave.
